changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/11806-login-server-unreachable.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/README.md` → `packages/app-shell/README.md` — edited by this change

  > `packages/app-shell/README.md` documents the two new states in its sign-up table. Its `useSignUpOffer` recipe for hosts now asks `decideSignUpOffer` only once the read has answered, and answers `unreachable` for a failed read.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `43e150518` (merge-base with origin/main): 24 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 335 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (342 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/38180736555)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4957032d3f33865f2a0bea71fcee9630f9b19cdc`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card objectui#12113 (body and all 5 comments, ruling 6105451919 and dev report 6114636335 included), PR objectui#12165 (body, 26-file list, three-dot diff against `main`), the check-runs on the head, and file contents at the head read through the API (the head's tree was also read in bulk, as a tarball, for the residual-reader sweep; nothing was built, run or re-run). The objectstack side was read at `main`: `studio.app.ts`, `account.app.ts`, `setup.app.ts`, `setup-nav.contributions.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies:

1. **The landing walk (`findFirstRoute`, `AppContent.tsx`) now takes a `component` entry as a landing**, beside object, page, dashboard and report, through the existing `buildItemRoute` to `@object-ui/layout`'s `resolveHref`. No second copy of the component URL rule was written. RIGHT: ruling A1 orders exactly this ("the landing resolver learns to walk `component` items") and the resolver is one function shared by every app, which is the only reading under which "like every other app's" holds. A Studio-only arm would have been the special case the ruling does not offer.
   - Studio: objectstack `main` `studio.app.ts` opens with `group_overview`, whose first child is `nav_app_builder`, `type: 'component'`, `componentRef: 'studio:builder'`, no `params`. `resolveHref`'s generic component branch gives `/component/studio/builder`, so the root navigates to `/apps/studio/component/studio/builder`; `AppContent` routes `component/:ns/:name/*` to `ComponentNavView`, and the console binds `studio:builder` to `BuilderLanding` (`registerStudioComponents.tsx`). The dev named the first item, as the ruling required. RIGHT.
   - Account: `account.app.ts` declares `nav_account_profile` (`component`, `account:profile_card`) first, before the Inbox group's `sys_inbox_message` view `mine`. The root moves from Notifications to Profile. The producer's own comment calls Profile "the canonical landing", and `AppHeader.tsx` records the old skip as a defect ("leaving the avatar menu's account entry dead"). Follows from A1 as written. RIGHT, and disclosed in the PR body and the changeset.
   - Setup: `group_overview` (gated `manage_platform_settings`) holds the `system_overview` dashboard, which the walk already took, so a platform admin lands where they did. For a caller without that permission, `group_apps` (ungated) opens with `nav_packages` (`component`, `developer:packages`), which the old walk skipped on its way to People and Organization's `nav_users`. The root moves from Users to Packages. Follows from A1 as written. RIGHT, and disclosed. (Contributions from packages other than `platform-objects` were not read here; the changeset's "as the platform declares it" hedge is the right width.)
   - Ruling: the Account and Setup landings are the ruling's own mechanism applied, not an excess. The ruling's premises did not name those two apps; the dev measured the blast radius (ablation: the component-first pin landed on `/apps/account/sys_inbox_message/view/mine` without the arm) and disclosed it instead of widening or hiding it, which is Prime Directive 10's shape. Not escalated.
2. **The app index route's last fallback is `null` instead of `StudioHomePage`.** An app that serves entries but no landing (every entry a `url`, `action` or `doc` link, or items only under `areas`) renders no page at its root and keeps its sidebar; the objectui#12079 empty state is not shown there, which is right because its sentence ("nothing available to you yet") would be false. Pinned (the `links` case). RIGHT.
3. **`appServesNoNavigation`**: comment only, no behaviour change. RIGHT.
4. **Sidebar**: the Studio-only Home row and `isStudioHomeActive` are gone; the package-scope memo stays for the package-management link, renamed `studioScopeSearch`, and the control pin shows that link byte-identical (`?package=`). The `Home` icon import stays and is still used by the Back-to-Home row. RIGHT.
5. **`AppPreview`**: comment and test name only. `findFirstLanding` already took any in-app href, `component` included, so the designer preview and the runtime now agree; the new preview pin holds the same order as the console pin. RIGHT.

Public-surface changes the diff implies:

6. **`StudioHomePage` leaves `views/metadata-admin/index.ts`.** That barrel is not the package entry: `@object-ui/app-shell`'s `exports` map is `.` and `./styles.css`; `src/index.ts` re-exports metadata-admin LEAF modules by name (DirectoryPage, ResourceRouter, ResourceListPage, ...) and never named `StudioHomePage` or the barrel; `views/index.ts` has no metadata-admin edge. Nothing published is removed. RIGHT: no public-surface change.
7. **22 `engine.home.*` strings leave the metadata-admin designer table** (`views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, en and zh). The table's `t` reaches out of the package only as the barrel's `translateMetadataAdmin`, which `src/index.ts` does not re-export, so it is internal. The removed set is the 19 keys the deleted page read plus 3 that had no reader before (`issuesHint`, `openDiagnostics`, `viewDomain`); `engine.home.recent` stays for `BuilderLanding`. At the head, `engine.home.` has exactly one reader left, `BuilderLanding.tsx`. The `@object-ui/i18n` en pack carries no `engine` namespace, so the packs and `TranslationKeys` are unchanged, as the dev found against the dispatch's H4 premise. RIGHT.
8. **Residuals**: at the head, `StudioHomePage` survives only in comments and test docblocks that describe the retirement, and in CHANGELOG history; `studio-home-page`, `isStudioHomeActive` and `studioHomeSearch` have zero occurrences; no non-test source links the bare `/apps/studio` root. RIGHT.
9. **Docs**: the console.md "Studio Package Scope" row and the README package-scope paragraph described the retired page and are reworded. The two "Studio home" rows kept in console.md, and README's "reached from the Studio home", quote "Not in a package" and "Installed (read-only, browsable)", which are `engine.studio.landing.*` strings of the `/studio` `BuilderLanding`, not the retired page. RIGHT to keep them.
10. **Tests**: the page's two tests deleted; five stubs lose the key (three console, two app-shell; the one-line touch in `AppContent.systemHubRoutes.test.tsx` is the whole of this diff's contact with epic objectui#7611's file, and the cross-lane note the claim promised is outside this record's inputs); the 12079 Studio control now asserts the landing (`/apps/studio/metadata` through `metadata:directory`) instead of the page; three new pins, with real `@object-ui/layout` in the console pin. RIGHT.

Gates on the head, 42 check-runs read at 2026-10-11T22:44:58Z: 34 completed with conclusion success (Build and E2E, Type Check, Lint, Test (dist pins), Spec Main Shape Gate, Bundle Analysis, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Changeset Declaration, Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Fixed Group Check, Changeset Claim Re-read, Changeset Overwrite Report, README Export Check, Docs Route Eager Closure Check, Pre-Install Import Graph Check, Line Citation Gate, Control Byte Scan, Shell Escape Residue Scan, Inert vi.mock Specifier Check, Action Ref Convention, Internal Docs Link Check, Build Docs, Doc Snippet Type Check, Doc Component Type Check, Doc Example Id Check, Doc Fence Language Check, Skill Example Check, Skill Guide Path Check, Skill Eval Token Check, Live E2E (informational), label, and Test shards 2/8, 4/8 and 5/8); 3 completed skipped (Test (coverage), Test (coverage shard), dependabot); 5 still in_progress with no conclusion at that read: Test shards 1/8, 3/8, 6/8, 7/8 and 8/8. No check-run has concluded failure. The open shards are the full test farm the dev left to CI; the verdict below is on the contract, and the landing waits on their green as it does for every PR.

Governed surfaces: none in the file list; "Governed Surface Queue Guard" green; head repo is the base repo (not a fork); the PR is a draft. `main` has moved three commits past the merge base (`faf4ce9` to `43e1505`); none touches this diff's source files, and `content/docs/guide/console.md` is touched by both in different rows (GitHub reports the PR mergeable, state `behind`). The queue leg re-merges.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/12113-retire-studio-home.md` declares `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`. RIGHT. The diff removes nothing from a published surface (item 6 and 7 above), moves no pack, and changes `TranslationKeys` by nothing; what it changes is runtime behaviour in a released package (where an app root lands), which owes a changeset and takes `patch`, the level objectui#12079's own landing change took. No `major` is declared. The body carries the Studio URL, the Account and Setup consequences, the url-only-app consequence and the string removal, each true at the head. The PR title's `feat(` prefix sets no level in this repo. `apps/console` is touched in tests only; the fixed group bumps together; "Changeset Declaration" and "Changeset Bump Policy" are green.
- **The edit to another card's pending changeset, `.changeset/12079-empty-nav-landing.md`**: one bullet, "The Studio app still opens on its own home ...", becomes "The Studio app, whose navigation is full, does not get the empty state. Where its root opens instead is objectui#12113: the app's first navigation entry." The 12079 entry is still pending at `main` `43e1505`, so both entries publish in the same release, and the old bullet would have gone false the moment this diff merged: the WENT FALSE class `scripts/check-changeset-claims.mjs` exists to surface (objectui#7721, objectui#8617). The new sentence is true in the tree it publishes from: `appServesNoNavigation` answers no for Studio's full navigation, and the root navigates to the App Builder. In proportion: one line; the front matter, the package names and every other claim of 12079 untouched; "Changeset Claim Re-read" and "Changeset Overwrite Report" (report-only) green. RIGHT.
- `Clause-②: no` in the PR body and the claim. RIGHT: no authorable surface widens or narrows (`component` was already an authorable navigation item type; the accepted set of landing types is a runtime walk, not a schema), and `TranslationKeys` is unchanged.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions: []` in the dev report; nothing to answer there. The dev's deviations, out-of-scope findings and acceptance notes, each:

1. Editing `.changeset/12079-empty-nav-landing.md`: answered under ②, in proportion.
2. `packages/app-shell/README.md` and the `AppPreview.docEntry-11197` test name beyond the claim's list: the README paragraph described the retired page and the test name listed the runtime's landing types; both are corrections the ruling's retirement implies. Answered.
3. app-shell run narrowed locally to 238 of 1270 files: the head's CI test shards are the measurement of record; their conclusions are in ①. Answered by the gates.
4. H4 premise false (no pack carries `engine.home.*`): verified at the head; no `@object-ui/i18n` entry is owed. Answered.
5. `main` merged before final verification, no force push: the head is the merge commit and the diff judged is the three-dot diff against `main`. Nothing to answer.
6. Two 429 interruptions: no bearing on the diff.
7. `AppHeader.tsx`'s Profile menu comment is now stale (the bare Account path does resolve to the component entry): the explicit link stays correct; a stale comment is not a defect and is outside the claim's surface; carrier none is right. Not escalated.
8. A url-only, action-only, doc-only or areas-only app now renders no page at its root: judged in ① item 2, pinned, no producer found in objectstack's examples or platform objects. Not escalated.
9. `resolveHref`'s generic `component` branch serialises `params` without `applyNavTemplate`: pre-existing, outside this card, and no producer (every templated Studio item is `metadata:*`, whose branch does resolve templates). A note, not a card, until a producer exists. Not escalated.
10. The Studio root loses the quick-find hint and the "Browse all metadata" button: the ruling retires the overview and its affordances with it; the directory keeps an in-app path (the "All types" breadcrumb on every metadata list and editor; `MetadataQuickFind` still mounted by `DirectoryPage`). Answered.
11. `Navigate` drops the root URL's query, so `/apps/studio?package=X` opens the App Builder unscoped: the same rule as every app's root, and at the head no non-test source links the bare Studio root with a query. Answered.
12. The ruling's second confidence gap (deployment deep links to the Studio root expecting the overview): unmeasured by the ruling and by the dev; the root still resolves, now to the App Builder. Not escalated.
13. Cross-seat note 6111306290 (objectui#12141 and #12146 wait on this PR's files): an ordering recorded on those cards, not a flag on this diff.
